critiques.issue: E060 is logged as 'supports H7.1.1', but it refutes it. The prediction put train accuracy in [0.82, 0.92] and said explicitly that 'Train accuracy ≥0.95 refutes N1'. Measured train accuracy was 0.964. Meanwhile H7 and H7.1 are still 'open' at 0.35-0.40. The follow-on inference also overreaches: the gap moved from 21.3 to 20.9 pp. That is 0.4 pp, on 5 dev seeds, with no SE, so it cannot show that the head-scale and BN-lr gains are a regularization effect. A 21 pp gap at 96% train accuracy is ordinary for CIFAR-100 and does not show the recipe is 'variance-limited'. E058 (losing 0.5 epoch at 32 px cost 0.24 pp dev) and E062 (removing one group-3 conv cost 0.89 pp) show that late steps and capacity still buy accuracy.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H7.1.1 refuted and lower H7 and H7.1. Do not treat E060 as permission to redirect all margin work to augmentation. Write the narrower finding as its own Lvl2: the early, low-res steps are saturated (E036, E063), but the late high-res steps (E058) and group-3 depth/capacity (E062, E044, E051) are not.

critiques.target: H6 (Lvl1 'accuracy capped near 75.3% by capacity/regularization, not optimizer settings')
critiques.issue: Results have already falsified this. The cap was broken by two optimizer and output-layer settings that change no capacity: head scale 2x (+0.44 pp dev, E053) and BN-bias LR 64x→32x→16x (+0.27 and +0.29 pp dev, E054 and E061). The dev mean went from 0.7534 to 0.7586 at lower time. H6 is still 'open 0.30', and its statement and H6.1 still describe the old ~75.3% ceiling and E033/E038 bases.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H6 refuted as stated. If capacity is still of interest, restate it on the 2/2/3 tip, e.g. 'group-2/3 width at equal epochs buys ≥X pp/s vs the 0.67 pp/s 32 px tail rate (E058)', and retire H6.1.1, H6.1.3 and H6.1.4. H6.1.4 is moot now that group 2 already has 2 convs.

critiques.target: Missing Lvl1/Lvl2: miscalibrated non-Muon parameter groups
critiques.issue: No current Lvl1 explains the largest margin gains since E030. The head logit scale and the BN-bias LR multiplier both set the effective step size and temperature of parameters that stayed on SGD after the Muon switch. Both were large and in the same direction, and the BN-bias trend is still monotone: each halving gained ~0.28 pp and the optimum has not been bracketed. H1.7.12 holds this only as a Lvl3 under a 'Muon settings' Lvl2, which misplaces it: the Muon knobs themselves (lr in E028, momentum in E040) were flat.
critiques.suggestion: Promote this to a Lvl2 under H1: 'SGD-group effective learning rates (BN bias, head, whitening bias) are mis-scaled under Muon + Lookahead + renorm.' Next tests, each on dev seeds 3-12 against the E061 dev mean: (1) BN-bias 8x, then 4x or 0x (frozen biases) to bracket the optimum; (2) head scale 1.5x and 3x re-swept at 16x, since both knobs plausibly interact through the logits; (3) SGD-group momentum 0.825 (Hiverge) and head lr 0.5x/2x, which have never been varied. All are time-free.

critiques.target: World model 'step cost concentrates in high-res group-1 layers' (H2.4, E004/E009 post-mortems, E059 'far more than its MACs share')
critiques.issue: A MAC count on the airbench layout (conv before pool, batch 1536, 32 px) contradicts this. Per forward step: group-1 conv2 128→128 at 16x16 ≈ 58 GMAC; group-2 conv1 128→384 at 16x16 ≈ 174 GMAC; group-2 conv2 384→384 at 8x8 ≈ 130 GMAC; group-3 conv1 384→576 at 8x8 ≈ 196 GMAC. The group-2/3 entry convs dominate. E059's −2.2 ms/step for one 130 GMAC conv is roughly MAC-proportional, not anomalous, and fits E044's +10%. The 'deep widening is nearly free' lesson came from SGD at batch 1024 (E004) and has been wrong since E044.
critiques.suggestion: Run one per-layer, per-phase profiler capture of the E061 tip (H2.6.3) and rebuild the cost model per conv, including the NS cost per weight shape. Then rank width cuts by MAC share. Group-2 width 384→320 shrinks three of the four biggest convs plus the NS matrices. Group-3 576→512 is the other candidate. Neither has been tried under Muon; the only width cut, E010, was on group 1 under SGD. Microbenchmark first.

critiques.target: H4 / H4.3 ('official seeds 0-2 run ~+0.15 pp above dev')
critiques.issue: Later data contradict this. Official minus dev mean: E053 −0.03, E054 −0.06, E055 −0.04, E056 −0.28, E057 +0.39, E058 −0.04, E059 +0.08, E061 −0.26, E063 −0.35, E048 −0.05, E049 +0.06, E050 +0.20, E051 −0.12. That is a mean near 0 with SD ≈ 0.2 pp. The +0.15 came from one recipe family, E038/E046. H4.5's licensing threshold, dev ≥0.7545 for P(official ≥0.753) ≈ 0.8, builds this bias in.
critiques.suggestion: Restate H4: official minus dev is a zero-mean residual with σ≈0.2 pp. Combined with dev-mean SE ≈0.08, an official ≥0.753 draw needs dev ≥ ~0.7558 for P≈0.9, or ~0.7547 for P≈0.8. At E061's dev 0.7586, the spendable margin is about 0.28 pp at 90% confidence. Budget the next time cuts against that number and drop the +0.15 offset.

critiques.target: H4.5.1, H1.1, H1 statement and other stale or mislabelled statuses
critiques.issue: Several nodes no longer match the evidence. H4.5.1 forecasts a stack (640 + pooling + bias window + 28 px tail) that was superseded by E055/E056. H1's text still talks about '~0.35 s of banked neutral cuts', which were spent in E055/E056. H1.9.1 shows 'open' with E063−, and E063 refuted it. H2.4.6 shows 'inconclusive' though E050 was logged as refutes. H2.3.2 is 'open' though E056 supports it. H1.3.4 is 'open' though E053 was a ~4 SE gain. H4.2 is 'inconclusive' though E019 refuted its only test. H1.3.3 is refuted but carries no evidence tokens (E038/E039). E058's description says '4 to 3.5 epochs at 32 px', but E056 was already at 3, and E059 lists 2.5x32, so the logged description is stale.
critiques.suggestion: Reconcile the statuses: refute H1.9.1; set H2.4.6 refuted; set H2.3.2 and H1.3.4 supported; set H4.2 refuted; add E038~/E039- to H1.3.3; retire H4.5.1. Correct E058's description to 3→2.5 so later exchange-rate calculations use the right schedule.

critiques.issue: Together, the results suggest an allocation story that no node states. Adding low-res epochs fails even with anchors fixed (E036, E063). Moving a 32 px epoch to 28 px costs little (E056, −0.08). Trimming the 32 px tail costs 0.67 pp/s (E058). So accuracy appears to be set by the late, high-res, low-LR steps. Two directions follow and neither has been tried. First, cutting low-res epochs (e.g. 2x20+2x24 or 1x20+3x24), which E063 implies is cheap. Second, reallocating saved low-res time to the 28/32 px tail. E031 (halving early steps via batch 3072) is not a clean counterexample, because it also changed the lr and batch.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl2 under H1/H2.3: 'early low-res epochs are saturated; marginal accuracy lives in the 28-32 px, low-LR tail.' Lvl3 prediction: on E061, dropping one 24 px epoch with warmup and Lookahead anchored in absolute steps saves ~0.35 s and costs <0.1 pp dev. Second prediction: spending that time on +0.5 epoch at 32 px is net-positive.

critiques.issue: None of the regularization nodes has been run in 63 experiments. That includes alternating vs random flip, which was inherited from CIFAR-10 and is the cheapest test in the tree. The E060 post-mortem now names regularization as the main lever, but on weak evidence (see the H7 critique). Two runs also contradict that framing: E026 (weaker low-res regularization) and E038/E039 (ls 0.4) were neutral.
critiques.suggestion: Run the flip test (H1.2.1) and one Cutout size (H1.3.2) on dev seeds as cheap, time-free probes, with pre-registered ±0.2 pp bands. Treat them as tests of the regularization view, not as the main margin plan. If both are null, regularization is not the binding axis.

critiques.target: H6.2.1 / H2.5.5 / H2.5.6 (orthogonalization quality vs cost)
critiques.issue: Two decisive failures (E035 −1.8 pp, E052 −2.1 pp) show accuracy is very sensitive to NS quality below the current budget. Nobody has tested whether the budget above is also under-saturated: AOL + 3 steps has never been run. The cheap, numerically near-equivalent Muon cuts (Gram reuse in H2.5.5, Gram-NS in H2.5.6, renorm every k steps in H2.5.3) are also all untested, even though Muon is now a larger share of a 5.24 s step.
critiques.suggestion: Run AOL+3 on dev seeds (H6.2.1). If it gains ≥0.2 pp for ~1-2% time, it is a better margin source than width. Check H2.5.5 in the code first, since it may be free. Run any Gram-NS variant only after an offline check on captured real gradients (the E035 lesson).

critiques.issue: E061's dev std was 0.13 pp, half the 0.22-0.30 seen elsewhere. That is probably chance. The '+0.29 pp' is about 2.3 SE on an unpaired difference, but it is one step in a sequence of chosen knob moves on the same 10 dev seeds. Repeatedly selecting on dev seeds 3-12 carries its own winner's curse (64x→32x→16x, head 2x), so the dev mean is no longer a clean held-out estimate.
critiques.suggestion: Keep using the pooled σ≈0.25-0.28 pp for SE, not E061's 0.13. Before spending the claimed ~0.55 pp of margin on aggressive time cuts, evaluate the E061 tip once on a fresh held-out seed block (e.g. seeds 13-22) to de-bias the dev mean, and keep that block out of selection.

critiques.issue: Nothing has tested this, yet it is still a Lvl1 at 0.45. The recent large wins (E058 tail, E059 depth cut) remove work and should transfer. The remaining candidate cuts (renorm every k, graph fusion, kernel swaps) are the overhead type H5.1 flags as fragile. Leaving it open adds nothing to decisions.
critiques.suggestion: Turn H5.1 into a ranking rule rather than a hypothesis: when two candidates are within ~2% locally, prefer the FLOP-removing one. Otherwise deprioritize H5 until an overhead-only cut is the deciding edit.

structured_output.summary: The tree has fallen behind the results. Since E053 the recipe moved from a dev mean of ~0.7534 at 6.68 s to 0.7586 at 5.24 s. The big gains came from changes the Lvl1 claims don't predict: two time-free settings on the parameters left on SGD after the switch to Muon (head logit scale, and a BN-bias LR whose optimum is still unbracketed), and cutting a group-2 conv. Four corrections are needed. E060 is logged as supporting H7.1.1, but by its own pre-registered rule (train accuracy ≥0.95) it refutes it. H6's '~75.3% cap, not optimizer' is falsified. H4's claim that the official seeds are favourable is contradicted by later runs (official minus dev ≈ 0 ± 0.2 pp). The cost model that says step time concentrates in group 1 is wrong by a simple MAC count: the group-2 and group-3 entry convs dominate. Several statuses are mislabelled or stale (H1.9.1, H2.4.6, H2.3.2, H1.3.4, H4.2, H4.5.1, and E058's description). Never tried: flip and Cutout, BN-bias below 16x, head scale re-swept at the new BN-bias LR, SGD-group momentum, AOL+3, cheaper Newton-Schulz variants, width cuts under Muon, and cutting low-res epochs. E036/E063 vs E058 suggest the early epochs are saturated while the high-res tail is not. Next steps: bracket the SGD-group learning rates on dev seeds; profile per layer and rank width cuts by MACs; trade low-res epochs for tail time; re-check the tip on a fresh held-out seed block before spending the ~0.28 pp of margin that holds at 90% confidence.
